name: Propanediol caprylate

lead: Propanediol caprylate is an ingredient in some shampoos and scalp treatments aimed at dandruff. People use these for a flake-free scalp and cleaner-looking hair.
It sits alongside actives like climbazole and zinc pyrithione in comparison studies.

paras: It is described as an antifungal agent against Malassezia yeasts on the scalp, which are associated with dandruff [1].
It is a topical cosmetic ingredient. Published safety and efficacy data specific to it are limited; irritation is a general consideration for any scalp product.

chain: Fewer flakes and a cleaner-looking scalp
angle.text: Used in anti-dandruff formulations, it targets the scalp yeast tied to flaking. People use such products to keep hair and shoulders free of visible flakes.

lead: Propanediol caprylate is an ester of propanediol and caprylic acid used in cosmetic and personal-care formulas, including anti-dandruff scalp products. For appearance, its role is as an antifungal ingredient aimed at Malassezia yeasts on the scalp, which are associated with dandruff and flaking, so that hair and scalp look cleaner and clearer of flakes [1].

Research on it is limited. A 2025 BMC Microbiology study used it as one of the conventional antifungal comparators, alongside climbazole, piroctone olamine, selenium sulfide and zinc pyrithione, when testing a chitinase and chitosanase combination against Malassezia species [1].

paras: It appears in scalp-care formulas as a newer ester-based alternative to classic dandruff actives, and was included among the standard antifungal agents in a 2025 comparison for dandruff-related Malassezia species [1].

No studies found. The related 2025 study was laboratory work in which propanediol caprylate served as a comparator against Malassezia furfur, restricta and globosa; its clinical part (n=18) tested a chitinase and chitosanase solution, not propanediol caprylate itself [1].
